title: Knowledge Graphs in Litigation Agents — Tom Smoker, WhyHow
talk_summary: Tom Smoker of WhyHow describes building litigation agents that combine multi-agent workflows with knowledge graphs to extract, structure, and query legal documents and web-scraped complaint signals. The core practical message is that chained probabilistic agents compound error, so he uses explicit schemas, graph-structured state, and ML filters to make each step testable and controllable.

takeaways.technique: Decompose workflows into IO-testable steps with explicit state
takeaways.what_they_do: Break a complex workflow into a specific set of steps, each with different requirements, frequencies, and state, and control that state explicitly rather than letting one big agent handle everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: break down a complicated white collar workflow down into a specific set of steps that I can IO test

takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly model that sequential chained agents multiply per-step accuracy, so a 5-step chain of 95% agents yields ~77% end-to-end success; use this to justify guardrails and human checkpoints.
takeaways.evidence_quote: five 95% accurate agents chained together sequentially. That's 77% expected accuracy
takeaways.numbers: 5 agents at 95% each → 77% expected end-to-end accuracy

takeaways.technique: ML filters instead of pure LLM filtering
takeaways.what_they_do: Use traditional ML/deterministic filters for qualification and reserve LLMs for gluing steps together, rather than relying on LLM judgment for every filter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very much for us not an LLM filtered system. It's an ML filtered system that LLMs have allowed us to pipe together

takeaways.what_they_do: Capture information state over time in a graph, then expand, prune, structure, and query it, so state is explicit and removable rather than buried in context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: capturing, expanding, pruning, structuring and then querying state for us happens in a graphical format

takeaways.technique: Schema-driven personalized filtering of noisy inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Scrape broad noisy sources, then apply per-client schemas to filter down to only the signals that matter, producing a specific report in a familiar form factor.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have schemas that we work with particular law firms and lawyers. And those schemas get us down to just the information that they care about

takeaways.what_they_do: Assume most agents are untrustworthy; spend effort on guardrails and only trust a small number of well-constrained agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Agents imply that these things are very capable. But I can write a bad prompt very easily and all of a sudden I have a bad agent
